_comment: Media source manifest. tools/media.py reads this and writes processed assets into /media/. Sources live outside the repository in _source/ and are never deployed.

scene-graph-itc.alt: A 3D scene graph over the ITC building second floor. A single building node at the top connects down to a room node, then to a dense band of place nodes following the corridor loop, then to object nodes scattered along the walls, and finally to the reconstructed mesh of the floor.
scene-graph-itc.caption: The layered scene graph over the ITC second floor. Look at the vertical structure: one building node, one room node, 1,349 place nodes tracing the corridor loop, and object nodes hanging off the walls. Counts by category are listed in the legend.

perception-pipeline.alt: Pipeline diagram. Monocular RGB enters M2H-MX on the GPU, producing depth and semantics. Those feed pose-aware temporal alignment and a CPU-side VIO that uses predicted depth, with IMU input. The result is a metric semantic mesh and a 3D scene graph with building, room, place, object, and mesh layers.
perception-pipeline.caption: One camera and one IMU in, a layered scene graph out. The two arrows returning from odometry into the perception block are the part that distinguishes this from a feed-forward pipeline: pose stabilises the next prediction rather than only consuming it.

mono-hydra-pp-pipeline.alt: Block diagram of the Mono-Hydra++ system showing perception, odometry, and mapping stages and the data passing between them.
mono-hydra-pp-pipeline.caption: Where each learned output enters the estimator.

scannet-radius.alt: Three floor plans side by side for ScanNet scene 0054. The first shows ground truth object centres as coloured dots, the second shows predicted object centres as squares, the third overlays them showing matched, missing, and unmatched objects.
scannet-radius.caption: Object placement on ScanNet scene 0054, scored by radius match at 0.5 m. Green is matched, orange is a ground-truth object the system missed, and a red cross is something it predicted that is not there. The aggregate figure is 42.59 percent, and this is what that number looks like.

scannet-failure.alt: Semantic mesh reconstruction compared against ground truth, showing small object classes absorbed into larger neighbouring surfaces.
scannet-failure.caption: A failure case. Small classes get absorbed into the dominant surface next to them, which the global mIoU of 44.96 percent does not show on its own.

uhumans2-loop.alt: Three trajectory plots on the uHumans2 dataset comparing ground truth against a baseline and against the system with depth sparse factors and a semantic mask, marking accepted, available, and missed loop closure candidates.
uhumans2-loop.caption: Loop closure behaviour on uHumans2. Of 233 candidates the baseline finds 212 and misses 21; adding depth sparse factors and the semantic mask shifts which candidates survive rather than simply finding more.

uhumans2-ablation.alt: Overview of the uHumans2 component ablation, showing trajectory and mapping quality across configurations.
uhumans2-ablation.caption: The component study. Different configurations win on different metrics, which is why no single one is presented as best.

m2h-mx-architecture.alt: M2H-MX architecture diagram. A DINOv3 backbone with LoRA adaptation feeds token reassembly and a feature pyramid, then register-gated Mamba blocks at each scale, task adaptors, a cross-task mixer, multi-scale convolutional attention, and finally the task heads.
m2h-mx-architecture.caption: M2H-MX. The backbone stays mostly frozen and LoRA adapts the later blocks, so the compute goes into the decoder and the cross-task exchange rather than into retraining the features.

m2h-mx-rgm.alt: The register-gated Mamba block. A global register vector passes through a linear layer and sigmoid to produce a channel-wise gate that modulates reshaped feature tokens before a Mamba block.
m2h-mx-rgm.caption: One global register vector gates every decoder scale. This is how global scene layout reaches local decoding without paying for full attention.

m2h-mx-ctm-msca.alt: Cross-task mixer followed by multi-scale convolutional attention, showing how auxiliary task features modulate a target task before spatial refinement.
m2h-mx-ctm-msca.caption: Cross-task mixing, then spatial refinement. Removing both costs 2.07 mIoU. Swapping the backbone costs 8.81, which is the more interesting number.

scenegraph-system-design.alt: System design diagram for monocular 3D scene graph construction, showing the perception networks, visual-inertial odometry, and the scene graph layers.
scenegraph-system-design.caption: The original Mono-Hydra design: two independent networks for depth and semantics, feeding a robocentric VIO and the Hydra scene graph layers.

itc-embedded.alt: Reconstruction of the ITC second floor produced from the embedded operating point on the Jetson Orin NX at reduced input resolution.
itc-embedded.caption: The same floor rebuilt from the Jetson operating point at 256x192. Mean error is 0.22 m here against 0.08 m at full resolution, which is the cost of running the perception on the drone.

wipe-rgb.alt: A corridor in the ITC building seen by the monocular camera: doors on the right, artwork on the walls, an orange floor receding into the distance.
wipe-rgb.label: RGB input

wipe-depth.alt: Predicted depth for the same corridor frame, rendered as a colour field where blue is near and red is the far end of the corridor.
wipe-depth.label: Predicted depth

wipe-semantics.alt: Predicted semantic labels for the same corridor frame, with flat colour regions for wall, floor, ceiling, and door.
wipe-semantics.label: Predicted semantics

itc-loop.alt: Screen recording of the scene graph being built while the drone flies the ITC second floor loop. The graph grows from nothing to a full corridor circuit, with live RGB, semantic, and depth views alongside.
itc-loop.caption: The scene graph forming over one loop of the ITC second floor, from the first frame to loop closure. Playback is 10x real time. Live RGB, predicted semantics, and predicted depth run down the right.

icra26.alt: Short clip of the M2H-MX perception front end driving the mapping pipeline.
icra26.caption: M2H-MX driving the mapping pipeline.

scope-explorer.alt: Simulated indoor exploration run showing the robot's occupancy map growing as it selects routes through the environment.
scope-explorer.caption: A 60 second excerpt of an exploration run in simulation, showing local and global behaviour as the occupancy map fills in.
